newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian parliament set to vote on new government.
newsitem.headline: Latvian parliament set to vote on new government.

text.p: Latvian Prime Minister Andris Shkele said on Wednesday that he had finished putting together a new government and would put it to a parliamentary vote on Thursday.
Shkele, a non-party businessman who has pledged to speed economic reforms and privatisation, is forming his second government, which includes eight parties.
"I plan tomorrow to hand in the governent declaration and the cabinet list for a vote," Shkele told reporters.
Shkele needs the backing of at least 51 members of the 100-seat parliament and political analysts expect the government to get the necessary backing.
Shkele said there were still three empty posts in the cabinet, which would be filled eventually by the largest party in parliament, the Democratic Party Saimnieks.
One of the vacant posts is that of finance minister, which Shkele said he or another minister would probably fill.
Shkele is forming his second government after resigning in January in the wake of a scandal over the nomination of a new finance minister.
Shkele quit after President Guntis Ulmanis called on parliament not to back Shkele's choice for finance minister, a businessman who had been investigated by the prosecutor's office.
The two leaders later settled their differences and the president recalled Shkele to the prime minister's post to form another government.
